profile.reading:
Iron Mountain Incorporated (NYSE: IRM) is a publicly traded REIT headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, whose core business is physical and digital records management; its data center division was built substantially through a January 2018 acquisition of IO Data Centers, which added facilities in New Jersey, Ohio, and two Arizona sites, not Virginia.

This building, VA-3, is part of Iron Mountain's 142-acre Northern Virginia data center campus in Prince William County. Per the operator's own site, the full campus currently comprises seven operational data centers, with a planned buildout of nine to ten buildings totaling more than 2,000,000 square feet and 400-plus MW of capacity, and Iron Mountain has separately acquired an adjacent 40-acre parcel for two further buildings totaling roughly 150 additional MW. Iron Mountain does not appear to publish its own dedicated VA-3 location page; this registry found none this session.

Aggregator Baxtel, used here as secondary corroboration only, describes VA-3 as the third and, at the time of that listing, largest building on the campus: more than 165,000 square feet, built in 2024, combining a two-story data center wing with a three-story office tower, with two 48 MW data halls of 30,000 square feet each and room designed in for four additional halls. VA-3's overall building IT capacity in MW was not disclosed on that source (held behind a paywalled dataset) and is not asserted here. Baxtel also gives VA-3's address as 11560 Hayden Road, differing from the 11640 Hayden Road already on file for this row; this registry has not been able to independently reconcile the two addresses against Prince William County property records this session, so both are noted rather than one being silently discarded. No independently verified Uptime Institute tier certificate was located for this building.

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 92 (Iron Mountain VA campus missing-address campaign): applied 11640 Hayden Rd, Manassas, VA 20109, from a reverse geocode corroborated by a coherent cross row street and numbering pattern across sibling VA rows. research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This Iron Mountain facility is part of the company data center business, which traces to a December 2017 purchase of IO Data Centers United States division for 1.3 billion dollars, acquiring four colocation data centers in New Jersey, Ohio, and Arizona, though this specific Virginia or Illinois location was not confirmed as part of that transaction in available sourcing this session. Iron Mountain itself was founded in 1951 as Iron Mountain Atomic Storage Corporation by Herman Knaust, a former mushroom entrepreneur who had purchased a depleted iron ore mine near Kingston, New York, went public in 1996, became a real estate investment trust in 2014, and as of 2023 is headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. The operators own current data center locations page describes its Northern Virginia presence as 400 plus MW across 142 acres in Manassas, and its own VA-1 and VA-2 solution guides separately describe an 83 acre campus that is the first of four planned campus data centers growing toward a nine facility, two million plus square foot development, confirming this is a real, large, multi building campus consistent with this registrys six separately numbered VA rows. This session resolved a street address for this specific VA-3 row. Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service returned 11640 Hayden Rd, Manassas, VA 20109 at 0.9 confidence, fitting the same coherent, evenly spaced Hayden Rd numbering sequence, 11600, 11640, 11680, found across sibling VA rows in this same batch, treated here as the corroborating check in place of a named press or aggregator source, which this session did not find. Given this, the session applies 11640 Hayden Rd as this rows address, flagged for a future researcher to confirm against a named source if one becomes available.

reading.body:
Iron Mountain VA-3's power capacity is unpublished, making it impossible to assess its role in Virginia's data center infrastructure or AI compute availability from public sources.

Iron Mountain operates a four-campus data center development in Manassas spanning 142 acres with 400-plus megawatts across the Northern Virginia region. This facility is one of six separately numbered buildings on that campus. Virginia hosts 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish power specifications. Among those with disclosed capacity, the state holds 1,375 megawatts total. Without a published megawatt figure for VA-3, no estimate of rack density, accelerator count, or actual compute power is possible.

The operator describes its Northern Virginia assets as a colocation platform but has not disclosed which tenants occupy this specific building. Colocation facilities serve multiple customers rather than a single AI developer or cloud provider, which shapes how their capacity converts to actual compute deployment. Virginia's infrastructure density and proximity to major population centers make it strategically important for data center placement, but capacity constraints or gluts cannot be assessed when operators do not publish their specifications.

This facility's actual contribution to AI scaling depends entirely on information Iron Mountain has chosen not to release: power delivery specifications, certification level, IT load density, and tenant identity. Tracking unpublished facilities matters because they represent real buildings with real power draws on the grid. The gap between what exists and what is known underscores how much of the infrastructure binding AI compute remains opaque to observers outside the operator.
